thread:
maria: Heads-up — error budget for model-serving-prod hit 95% burn after last night's capacity churn. Observability quick dump below.

ops-bot: ALERT: model-serving-prod SLO burn_rate > 20x for 30m :rotating_light: <https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/model-serving-slos?orgId=1>

jon: can you paste the PromQL used for burn rate? I'm trying to correlate with gpu-saturation spikes.

maria: sure. We compute 30m burn rate vs 14d windows. PromQL snippet:
```
# SLI: successful_requests_ratio over 14d and 30m
sli_14d = sum(rate(requests_total{job="model-serving",status!~"5.."}[14d])) / sum(rate(requests_total{job="model-serving"}[14d]))
sli_30m = sum(rate(requests_total{job="model-serving",status!~"5.."}[30m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{job="model-serving"}[30m]))
burn_rate = (1 - sli_30m) / (1 - sli_14d) / (30m/14d)
```
(we actually compute via recording rules but pasted raw for context)

ash: thanks. I can see GPU pod restarts in cluster logs around 02:10 UTC — possibly a driver upgrade rolled across the nodepool. Crashloop and node-recycler kicked in.

devon: confirmed. Nodepool `gpu-a` had a rolling upgrade due to security patch; DaemonSet for nvidia-driver updated. Chart shows 3x pod evictions in us-west-2 for 02:05-02:20.

maria: SLO defs we use today are:
- error budget for availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for model-serving-prod
- latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for inference requests
- saturation SLO: GPU core utilization < 80% avg per-pool

jon: can we tighten alerting to avoid noisy burns when we have planned maintenance events? Maybe suppress or route to maintenance schedule.

ash: propose 2 changes:
1) Add maintenance windows tag to alerts: `maintenance=true` so PagerDuty doesn't fire
2) Introduce a 'grace' rule: ignore burn_rate > 10x if nodepool_rolling_update_active == 1

maria: agreed. For (2) here's a suggested PromQL for mute condition:
```
nodepool_rolling = max_over_time(nodepool_update_active{pool=~"gpu-.*"}[1h])
mute_burn = nodepool_rolling > 0
```

devon: also recommending we separate SLOs by region. us-west-2 and eu-central-1 have different SLAs and capacity constraints; error budget should be tracked per-region to avoid single-region storms blowing global budget.

jon: good call. Also cost note — when we overprovision GPU during rollback we burn budget/cost. Ops request: add a Grafana panel showing cost-per-error-budget-burn (approx). I'll wire up a simple computation using spot vs reserved instance billing.

maria: action items:
- @jon update alerting rules to add maintenance tag and mute logic (ETA 4h)
- @ash add per-region SLO dashboards and update recording rules (ETA 1d)
- @devon investigate nodepool rolling upgrade process to avoid simultaneous evictions (ETA 2d)
- @sre-oncall follow up on any oncall pings and confirm postmortem if needed

sre-oncall: ack. I'll collect incident timeline and link to postmortem when ready. Also suggest adding a runbook step to scale down traffic or fallback to smaller model variants during capacity churn.

maria: thanks team. saving the Grafana URL here: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/model-serving-slos?panel=3

jon: FYI I trimmed some alerts thresholds to reduce pager fatigue. Will post diff in PR.

ash: looks good. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0012 — high SLO burn for model-serving-prod. Assigned to oncall.

maria: closing thread here; will reopen if burn continues after mitigations.
